question: What are the graduation requirements for the Computer Science major?
answer: The Computer Science major requires students to complete a total of 8 credits, which can be divided into 6 courses. First, students must complete one programming course, which is either CS 101: Introduction to Programming, CS 103: Programming for Data Science and Visualization, or CS 104: Introduction to Computer Science. Next, they must take one 100-level or 200-level CS course. Students can choose one of these courses, and they may also take a computer science course (MATH 202 - Discrete Math) as part of a team. The student must also complete 4 credits of computer science-related courses, with a minimum of 4 credits from the foundational courses listed in the context. For example, they can select either CS 201 – Data Structures & Algorithms or CS 215: Algorithms and Data Structures. To formally declare a minor in Computer Science, students must complete at least one Computer Science course (MATH 202 - Discrete Math is also counted) and pass a final exam. Students will gain employment in Vietnam as software engineers, in the U.S. as AI engineers, and in other countries as data engineers, business analysts, product owners, product development managers, and many other roles.
